chunks: Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Hammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him saying: 'There is nothing except that in it there is a Book or a Sunnah.'

key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: Sunnah — the established practice and sayings of the Prophet and the Imams, the second foundational source
key_terms.كِتَابٌ: the Book — referring to the Quran, the primary source of Islamic law and guidance

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the comprehensiveness of the Quran and Sunnah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) asserts the comprehensive nature of Islamic guidance, stating that every matter — whether pertaining to the permissible, the forbidden, or any aspect of life — has been addressed either in the Quran (the Book) or the Prophetic and Imamic Sunnah. This hadith is a foundational principle in Shia jurisprudence, affirming that no situation is left without divine guidance. The Imam's audience — his close companions and scholars of jurisprudence — would have understood this as an injunction to always seek rulings within these two sources rather than resorting to arbitrary opinion.

en.hubeali: Ali, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Hammad, from Abu Abdullahasws, said,
‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is none from the things except that with regards to it -there is (something in the) Book or a Sunnah’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali has narrated from Muhammad ibn “isa from Yunus from Hammad from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“There is no case for which there is not a law in the book or the Sunnah, the noble tradition of the holy Prophet (s.a.)”
